subtopics.title: Choosing the Ratio, and Finding a Side on Top

questions.question: Which side of a right-angled triangle NEVER changes its name when you switch angles?
options: The hypotenuse — it always faces the right angle

questions.question: A 15 m ladder leans at 50° to the ground. The height it reaches uses which ratio?
options: Sine — the height is opposite the angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse

questions.question: The ladder height works out to 15 × sin 50° = 11,49 m. Which sense check confirms it?
options: 11,49 is an odd-looking number, so it must be right
The answer matches the ladder's length
At 45° the ladder would reach about 10,6 m; 50° is steeper, so slightly higher is correct — and the answer stays below the 15 m hypotenuse

questions.question: Why can the OPPOSITE side never exceed the hypotenuse?
options: Because the opposite is always horizontal
Because sine of any acute angle is less than 1, and opposite = hypotenuse × sine
It can exceed it in obtuse triangles

questions.question: For the guy wire: cos 55° = 20/wire. Freeing the unknown requires:
options: Dividing the known side by the ratio: wire = 20 ÷ cos 55°

questions.question: A learner computes the wire as 20 × cos 55° = 11,47 m. What convicts this instantly?
options: The hypotenuse must be the LONGEST side, yet 11,47 is shorter than the 20 m it must exceed

questions.question: The rule for the unknown's position is:
options: Unknown on top: divide; unknown underneath: multiply
Unknown on top: multiply; unknown underneath: divide the known side by the ratio

subtopics.title: Finding Angles, and Solving the Whole Triangle

questions.question: The ramp rises 1,2 m over a 4 m run. Its angle comes from:
options: tan⁻¹ of 0,3 — inverse tangent of rise over run — giving 16,70°

questions.question: The triangle's third angle is found by:
options: 90° − 16,70° = 73,30°, since the two acute angles of a right triangle sum to 90°

questions.question: The ramp surface (the third side) is best computed by:
options: Pythagoras: √(1,44 + 16) = 4,18 m — exact, with no inherited rounding error

questions.question: Why must full calculator accuracy be kept until the final line?
options: Because calculators cannot store rounded numbers
Because rounding an intermediate value (like the angle to 17°) visibly shifts every later answer

questions.question: Both elevation and depression are ALWAYS measured from:
options: The horizontal — never from the vertical

questions.question: The angle of depression from a lighthouse top equals the angle of elevation from the ship because:
options: The two horizontals are parallel, making them alternate angles
The sea is flat only near lighthouses

questions.question: The water tower: 30 m away, eyes 1,5 m up, elevation 58°. The tower's height is:
options: 30 × tan 58° + 1,5 = 49,51 m — the eye height is added back

questions.question: From a 60 m lighthouse, depression 20° to a ship. The ship's distance from the base is:
options: 60 ÷ tan 20° = 164,85 m — the unknown adjacent sits underneath, so divide

subtopics.title: Naming the Sides from Where You Stand

questions.question: In the yard picture, choosing your angle FIRST matters because:
options: Opposite and adjacent swap places when you move to the other corner — labels written before choosing are unreliable
The hypotenuse changes name as you move
The diagonal gets longer as you walk
It is only a style preference

questions.question: The whole ratio decision uses:
options: Only two sides — the one you know and the one you want; the rest is noise

questions.question: Opposite paired with adjacent calls which ratio?

subtopics.title: Upstairs You Multiply, Downstairs You Divide

questions.question: The airtime picture: one voucher costs R30, so twelve cost 12 × 30; twelve cost R360, so one costs 360 ÷ 12. The lesson for trig is:
options: The missing number decides whether you multiply or divide — same relationship, opposite moves

questions.question: In cos 55° = 20/wire, the unknown is 'downstairs', so:
The free safety net after solving for a hypotenuse is:
options: Checking the answer is a whole number
Checking the angle is less than 45°
Confirming the hypotenuse is the biggest number in the triangle — if not, the fraction was flipped

questions.question: When a depression angle confuses you, the rescue move is:
options: Walk yourself to the bottom of the picture and use the same number as an ELEVATION — alternate angles guarantee they match

questions.question: The learner's triangle at the water tower starts at:
options: Her EYES — so the 1,5 m below the triangle must be added back at the end

questions.question: The question to ask at the end of every elevation problem is:
options: Is the answer bigger than 100 m?
Did my triangle start at ground level, or above it?
Did I use all three sides?

questions.question: The Port Shepstone result — 164,85 m across open water, measured from the tower — illustrates:
options: That lighthouses must be exactly 60 m tall
That ships stay close to shore
The whole point of trigonometry: measuring distances you cannot physically reach
